chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"It is obligatory for the Sa'ir (one who shaves his head) to shave, and if he has already performed Hajj, if he wishes he may trim, and if he wishes he may shave. But if he has tied up his hair or trimmed it, then shaving is obligatory upon him and trimming is not sufficient for him."

key_terms.الصَّرُورَة: The Sa'ir: A pilgrim who is forced to cut his hair due to an impediment, requiring him to shave his head rather than just trim.
key_terms.عَقَصَهُ: To trim or cut the hair.
key_terms.لَبَّدَ: To tie up or bind the hair.
key_terms.يَقْصُر: To trim (the hair, not shaving completely).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who shaves his head (Sa'ir) regarding whether he must shave again or if trimming is sufficient?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific penalty for a pilgrim who prematurely shaves or trims their hair before the designated time, distinguishing between the initial act and the final completion of the ritual. It establishes that while the pilgrim retains the option to either shave (*halq*) or trim (*taqsir*) initially, a subsequent choice to trim necessitates a mandatory full shave to rectify the status, ensuring the complete removal of hair as required for the release from *ihram*. This ruling highlights the juristic precision in Shia fiqh regarding the sequence of actions and their corresponding legal consequences during Hajj.
